artifacts.title: Myers v. Illiana Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.synopsis: Seven members of a PCA mission church were tried and censured by a provisional Session for opposing the organizing minister's continuation as permanent pastor. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the convictions, holding that the indictments lacked required specificity under BCO 32-5, that the accused had no sinned against the fifth or ninth commandment by expressing opinions about ministerial suitability, and that the right to choose a pastor belongs to the congregation—not the provisional Session. A concurring opinion addressed indictment requirements, standard of review in appeals, and congregational rights in mission church minister selection.

artifacts.title: Herron et al. v. Central Indiana Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied most specifications of a complaint filed by TE Herron and others against Central Indiana Presbytery's investigative and suspension procedures, but sustained the complaint on the point that Presbytery improperly denied Herron access to Presbytery minutes while under process. The decision includes extensive discussion of pre-trial BCO 43-1 complaints ('interlocutory appeals') and the proper scope of BCO 31-10 administrative suspensions.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Neal Ganzel appealed his conviction and six-month suspension by Central Florida Presbytery for abuse of spiritual authority and related charges. The SJC unanimously sustained both specifications of error, finding that CFP violated BCO 32-20's one-year statute of limitations for most charges and committed numerous procedural missteps that rendered the disciplinary process significantly flawed and prejudicial, reversing the entire censure.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Tarter appealed his deposition by Evangel Presbytery's Judicial Commission for failure to submit to presbytery authority. The SJC sustained multiple specifications of error — including that the Presbytery's committee had no authority to make certain demands, the indictment was inadequate, and hearsay evidence was improperly admitted — and remanded the case to Evangel Presbytery for constitutionally compliant process or dismissal.

artifacts.title: William G. Mitchell v. The Presbytery of the Ascension
artifacts.synopsis: RE Mitchell appealed his indefinite suspension from office as Ruling Elder by the Presbytery of the Ascension, arising from allegations he broke a promise to take a sabbatical from Session and failed in his duties as Clerk of Session. The SJC vacated the judgment on Specification No. 2 (promise-breaking) and remanded for possible new trial, and reversed and dismissed Specification No. 6 (clerk duties) as insufficiently serious to warrant trial.

artifacts.title: Chastain v. Heritage
artifacts.synopsis: Appeal of TE Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery. Chastain challenged Heritage Presbytery's judgment of guilty on charges of divisive behavior and censure of indefinite suspension from office and sacraments. The SJC sustained Presbytery's judgment, finding that Chastain's public letters to the congregation expressing disagreement with Session decisions violated his ordination vows to be subject to his brethren and maintain the peace and unity of the Church, even though his underlying views were not sinful.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Michael Chastain appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension by Heritage Presbytery for divisive behavior, arising from his public letters to his congregation disagreeing with Session actions regarding an associate pastor call and a related Christian school controversy. The SJC denied the appeal (20-1), upholding the conviction and censure while finding procedural errors that did not rise to reversible level; a dissent by RE Frederick Neikirk argued the charge of 'divisive behavior' failed BCO 29-1's requirement that offenses be proven from Scripture.

artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church complained that Louisiana Presbytery improperly assumed original jurisdiction over church member Mike Holland, barring him from the Lord's Table for contumacy after he was cited in SPLC reporting regarding Auburn Avenue Presbyterian Church. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that because Delhi Session had investigated and acted under BCO 31-2, Louisiana Presbytery lacked grounds to assume original jurisdiction under BCO 33-1, rendering its judgment against Holland a nullity; three dissenting opinions argued the SJC lacked appellate review of the jurisdiction question because no timely complaint was filed against the assumption of jurisdiction itself.

artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Grace Reformed Presbyterian Church appealed its conviction for contumacy and termination of its relationship with Heartland Presbytery. The SJC reversed the conviction, holding that a presbytery lacks original jurisdiction to indict and try a session (lower court) for an offense such as contumacy, as BCO provisions reserve original jurisdiction over ruling elders to the Session level.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Robert Hopper challenged James River Presbytery's restriction on teaching and preaching about present-day prophecy and tongues. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that presbytery may limit such teaching for the welfare of the church when it determines the views threaten the church's peace or purity, while declining to issue a comprehensive doctrinal ruling.
